program.merge_policy: accumulate twenty 25-finding deep passes; consolidate and run heavy validation after Wave 2500

source_provenance: Direct PubMed/NCBI discovery and abstract verification
PMID-level dedupe against cumulative Wave 2000 index and rolling deep-state

waves.focus: Meta-analysis of 15 RCTs found oral magnesium supplementation did not significantly improve insulin or HOMA-IR in diabetes or prediabetes; dose and duration subgroups remained null, while baseline insulin resistance may modify response.

Meta-analysis of RCTs found Ashwagandha significantly lowered cortisol but did not significantly improve perceived-stress scores; this biomarker–symptom disconnect and moderate heterogeneity limit claims of broad stress relief.

Large meta-analysis of magnetic-resonance-spectroscopy studies found modestly elevated brain choline signals and greater variability in several psychosis-spectrum groups, especially treatment-resistant cohorts; this is biomarker evidence, not evidence for or against choline supplementation.

Meta-analysis in rugby players found small improvements in sprint performance and perceived exertion and a large but heterogeneous passing-accuracy signal, with no significant strength, jump, metabolic, or hormonal effects; certainty ranged from low to very low and sleep/recovery concerns were noted.

Systematic review of 14 RCTs found whey protein may help preserve fat-free mass during weight loss in adults with obesity, especially alongside resistance exercise or anabolic-enriched formulations, but several trials were neutral and overall certainty was limited by heterogeneity and small samples.

Meta-analysis of diabetes trials found omega-3 had no significant pooled effects on triglycerides, LDL/HDL, HbA1c, fasting glucose, or inflammatory/oxidative markers; fasting insulin, HOMA-IR, and corneal nerve branch density improved, but evidence certainty was very low to low and findings were hypothesis-generating.

Meta-analysis of 26 studies found creatine increased serum creatinine and lowered creatinine-based estimated GFR, but did not reduce Cr-EDTA-measured GFR or worsen urea, albuminuria, or proteinuria; changes likely reflect creatinine metabolism rather than kidney injury.

Network meta-analysis of 18 pediatric RCTs found acute-otitis-media prevention varied strongly by probiotic strain; CBA-L74 retained a robust benefit after sensitivity analysis while some other strain signals attenuated, underscoring strain-specific rather than class-wide efficacy.

Meta-analysis of 8 RCTs in postmenopausal women found green tea reduced ghrelin but not overall leptin, adiponectin, or insulin; subgroup signals were highly heterogeneous with some publication-bias concerns and should not be converted into dose prescriptions.

Meta-analysis of 27 RCTs found perioperative vitamin C reduced acute postoperative pain, opioid consumption, rescue analgesia, and early nausea/vomiting, but heterogeneity and publication bias limit certainty and evidence was insufficient for routine clinical recommendation.

Meta-analysis of 47 observational studies found ferritin-defined iron status was not significantly associated with thyroid hormones in pregnancy, while lower hemoglobin correlated with higher TSH and lower free T4; associations do not establish an iron-supplement treatment effect.

Single-arm meta-analysis found vitamin D deficiency was common in published ataxia-telangiectasia cohorts, with about half below 20 ng/mL; prevalence data support monitoring but do not establish supplementation efficacy.

Meta-analysis of 12 studies reported better response, nasal symptoms, IgE, quality of life, and fewer adverse reactions with Chinese herbal medicine for allergic rhinitis; heterogeneous multi-herb interventions prevent ingredient-level or generic-herb claims.

Meta-analysis of 11 studies found intrathecal magnesium added to bupivacaine reduced shivering and prolonged sensory/motor block without significant increases in hypotension, nausea/vomiting, pruritus, or bradycardia; evidence is anesthesia-route specific.

Meta-analysis of 6 RCTs found IV magnesium used adjunctively for fast atrial fibrillation favored rate control and showed a non-significant rhythm-conversion trend, while flushing increased markedly; the evidence is intravenous acute-care therapy, not oral magnesium supplementation.

Meta-analysis of five studies in type 2 diabetes found saffron supplementation reduced TNF-alpha but did not significantly change CRP, IL-6, IL-10, MDA, or total antioxidant capacity; the evidence base remains small.

Meta-analysis of 8 RCTs found Ginkgo biloba extract improved fasting glucose, HOMA-IR, several inflammatory markers, and some anthropometric measures but not HbA1c or lipid profile; small effects, heterogeneity, publication bias, short follow-up, and minor liver-enzyme elevations make the findings preliminary.

Meta-analysis found a small average ergogenic effect of acute caffeine in women, but no clear moderation by menstrual-cycle phase or hormonal-contraceptive status; certainty was low to very low and evidence does not support rigid phase-specific caffeine prescriptions.

Systematic review found mixed topical, systemic, and biomarker evidence suggesting potential dermatologic roles for L-carnitine, but interventions varied widely and dermatology-specific trials are insufficient to establish broad oral-supplement efficacy.

Meta-analysis of cohort studies found no significant association between higher dietary omega-3 or omega-6 intake and breast-cancer risk overall; a small regional omega-6 subgroup signal was observational and not evidence for supplementation.

Systematic review/meta-analysis found no robust overall ergogenic or physiological benefit of CoQ10 in athletes, including neutral VO2max and most biomarker outcomes; a favorable MDA sensitivity-analysis signal was fragile amid heterogeneity and methodological limitations.

Meta-analysis of 19 pediatric RCTs found prebiotics, probiotics, and synbiotics produced no clinically important improvements in hemoglobin, hematocrit, ferritin, or anemia overall; serious adverse events were not reported.

Narrative toxicology review concluded turmeric is generally low-risk under standard conditions but high concentrations, prolonged use, and certain formulations have produced hepatic, oxidative, or genomic toxicity signals; much of the concerning evidence is preclinical, so human thresholds remain uncertain.

Meta-analysis found lower serum zinc and selenium in children with drug-resistant epilepsy and inconsistent copper differences; substantial heterogeneity and observational designs prevent causal or supplementation conclusions.

Meta-analysis of 15 RCTs found IV iron corrected pregnancy anemia faster and produced fewer adverse events than oral iron, while neonatal outcomes and individual maternal complications did not significantly differ; this is route-comparative clinical-treatment evidence.
